geometry_edits.rationale: Keep the dominant mass as a bent bar, but increase the clarity of the bend so the primary gesture reads more strongly in all views.
A stronger bend should better articulate the access edge and produce a more coherent public-facing turn in plan and elevation.
Slightly finer subdivision should support a more continuous stepped profile without breaking the mass into fragments.
Increase setback depth modestly to emphasize a legible upper hierarchy while preserving the primary street datum.
Maintain a controlled lateral shift so the stepped upper mass reads as one continuous section rather than stacked fragments.

graph_edits.rationale: Turn the primary bar into a more legible bent ribbon so the dominant gesture better tracks the site edge and creates a clearer public threshold.
Keep the dominant bar aligned as the main organizing datum while the bend sharpens the frontage response.
Deepen the carved void so the ground response is more publicly legible from the access edge.
Widen the subtraction to read as a usable court or entry seam rather than a narrow notch.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass across views: a compact bent bar with a stepped upper condition. It is not especially elegant, but it avoids the failure of being coherent in only one view, and the silhouette remains a single family rather than colliding solids. The main weakness is the public edge: the blue frontage is acknowledged only weakly by a small seam/undercut, so the open-space figure is present but not strongly legible. Programmatically, the mass plausibly supports neighborhood living / active ground use better than a pure object because it keeps a street-building scale and a controlled void. The stepped upper form is acceptable as a capacity-aware section, not merely arbitrary tiering, though it remains slightly generic. Overall it passes the hard program gate, but would benefit from a clearer access-facing carve or court and a cleaner anchor at ground.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact street-facing massing can still support neighborhood-commercial use if it preserves a clear ground threshold and calm upper datum.
Filtered edges and courtyard-like outdoor rooming can strengthen the public edge without fragmenting the mass.
A small program can gain spatial identity through a controlled subtraction rather than through added fragments.
